newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks close lower, ITC plunges six pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks close lower, ITC plunges six pct.

text.p: Blue-chips posted small losses at Bombay bourses on Tuesday amidst a dull undertone, with market action focussed on ITC, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 29.88 points, or 0.97 percent. to 3,062.84 after rising to 3,104.03 in mid-session.
"The market sentiment is pretty weak. There isn't any major buying support seen in share prices," said dealer Vetri Subramaniam at local brokerage SSKI Securities.
ITC stock plunged 18.25 rupees to 269.0 rupees on volumes of 2.7 million shares traded at the BSE.
Dealers said heavy offloading in the stock by local speculators on the last day of settlement at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) pulled down prices.
The share was down 19.60 rupees at 270.40 at the NSE.
The tobacco conglomerate is being investigated for alleged "violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million," according to the finance ministry.
Last week, the Enforcement Directorate searched the firm's offices and arrested senior officials including two former chairmen.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net sellers at the end of October, latest data available from the exchange showed.
According to the daily figures released by the BSE, FIIs sold shares totalling 500 million rupees in the last three days of October and bought shares totalling 240 million.
On November 1, FIIs were net sellers of 50 million rupees.
TISCO lost 6.25 to 165.50, SBI 3.50 to 215.0, Reliance 3.75 to 185.0, TELCO 12.20 to 395.75 and ACC 26.0 to 1,430.0.
